testcase.name: N14-b: a skipped block touching the request is on the truncation face
touching is also six-faced: an element only cornering the face keeps its verdict
N14-c: the element against the missing base is withheld, the far one is not
the portal case from #74: the surviving column is withheld, the far one is not
an element is withheld when ANY of its blocks touches the face, not only the first
an empty request cannot be truncated by anything
the face keeps the order it was given, so reported examples are stable
N14-e: nothing skipped means nothing to say
no face means no element is withheld, whatever was solved
a skipped block nowhere near the request is a different structure, not a truncation
adjacency is the six faces: a diagonal neighbour carries no load path
ids are reported, not indices — the packet identifies elements by id
all six faces are checked, none forgotten
